title: LOW BACK, MID-BACK & HIP FLEXOR PAIN, MOBILITY & CONTROL PROTOCOL
tagline: 6-Week Progressive Eccentric, Glute-Driven & Full-Range Integration System
goal:
This protocol restores mobility and reduces pain in the low back, mid-back, hips, and pelvis by addressing:
Glute inhibition
Hip flexor tone
Posterior chain stiffness
Thoracolumbar control
Loss of usable range of motion
The system prioritizes:
Glute-driven spinal unloading
Eccentric length under control
Hip flexor decompression
Full-range motion integration
Long-term maintenance through movement

principles.title: ⚠️ MOST IMPORTANT RULE — READ FIRST
principles.text:
THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS ENTIRE PROTOCOL.
IF THIS RULE IS NOT FOLLOWED CONSISTENTLY, THE REST OF THE PROGRAM WILL NOT HOLD AND PAIN WILL RETURN.

principles.title: GLUTES MUST BE “ON” — ALL DAY, EVERY DAY
principles.text:
The glutes must remain lightly engaged at all times, even when you are not exercising.
Target:
5-10% effort
Gentle background tension
Never a hard squeeze
Think of the glutes as idling, not contracting.
❌ Do NOT fully relax the glutes while sitting
❌ Do NOT rely on the low back for posture
❌ Do NOT wait until pain appears to engage them

principles.title: WHEN THIS APPLIES (ALL THE TIME)
principles.text:
This applies while:
Sitting
Standing
Walking
Transitioning positions
Lifting
Exercising
Training
Every movement is part of the protocol.

principles.title: KEY CUE (MEMORIZE THIS)
principles.text:
“My glutes are always on — just enough.”
This rule continues permanently, even after the 6-week protocol ends.
This is how pain stays gone.

principles.title: IMPORTANT SENSATION & SAFETY NOTICE
principles.text:
Some discomfort is expected during eccentric and length-based work.
STOP IMMEDIATELY if you experience:
Sharp spinal pain
Loss of leg strength
Progressive numbness or tingling
Pain that worsens for more than 24 hours

guidelines:
The movements taught in this program must be integrated into:
Strength training
Conditioning
Daily movement
They are not optional.

As long as:
Glutes remain lightly active
Full-range motion is respected
Pain should not return.
callouts:

This is motor control + tolerance restoration.
